items.title: Sheffield's Sister Wives announce new album Heavy Set with laugh-cry single “Hairless Whisper” | The Line of Best Fit
items.summary:
“Hairless Whisper” is a rager against late-stage capitalism with an laugh built into the title. Love said "it’s about the mounting personal and systemic cost of capitalism... rejecting how a person's worth and value is mainly measured through productivity and achievement." [...] Scuzzy psych-pop quartet Sister Wives have detailed their second album, Heavy Set, due 5 February via Redundant Span Records. Lead single “Hairless Whisper” is out now.

The quartet's follow-up to their 2023 debut Y Gawres – which was nominated for the Welsh Music Prize – was recorded with producer James Atkinson at The Stationhouse in Leeds. The band said the record moves into heavier territory, with all four members sharing songwriting, vocals, and lyric-writing. [...] Rose Love explained that the title came from assembling a set list of heavy songs. “But it’s also something that specifically women get called.” Rachael Loomes added that “we were trying to shift the meaning of it and take ownership, as it's quite a derogatory term.”

items.title: Bart Verbruggen to Liverpool - will it happen? Football Whispers Index scores Brighton transfer chances
items.summary:
The usual assumption in a move like this, a typically Premier League mid-table side losing a player to one of the league's grandest names, does not hold up cleanly when the selling club is currently placed above the buyer.

Verbruggen is not escaping a bench or a rotation fight either; he is Brighton's nailed-on starter, so any move to Liverpool would have to be sold to him on status and history rather than first-team certainty. [...] It stalls if Brighton's £50m valuation holds, or if Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Chelsea or Manchester United move first.

This is a rumour built on a contract date rather than a negotiation, and that is worth remembering before anyone gets carried away with it.

The strongest case for Liverpool is that Verbruggen's form this season gives them a concrete, data-backed reason to want him, not just a name plucked from a wider market. [...] Romano's own framing matters here, since he stopped short of calling Alisson's departure certain, which keeps this whole rumour a step removed from genuine urgency.

The save-percentage gap between Verbruggen and Alisson this season is not marginal, and it is exactly the kind of form curve that makes a club start planning a succession even before a contract has actually expired.
